issues.title: Documented "SameSite=None requires Secure=True" cookie invariant is not enforced at startup
issues.body:
`docs/admin_docs/security/securing_superset.mdx:98-100` tells operators to set
`SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE = 'None'` for iFrame embedding, and then states the requirement:

> Setting SameSite to 'None' requires that SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE is also set to True.

Nothing enforces it. `grep -rn "SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE" --include="*.py" superset/` returns
two hits — the default at `config.py:2854` and `superset/mcp_service/mcp_config.py:225`.
There is no validation anywhere.

The shipped defaults are `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = False` (`config.py:2853`) and
`SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE = "Lax"` (`:2854`). An operator who follows the embedding note and
sets `SameSite = "None"` without also setting `Secure` gets a configuration that is both
insecure by the project's own written rule and silently broken: `SameSite=None` without
`Secure` is invalid per RFC 6265bis, and Chromium, Firefox and Safari reject the `Set-Cookie`
outright. The session cookie is dropped by the browser, login fails, and there is no
server-side signal explaining why.

Fix: validate at startup, in two tiers, as a new `check_cookie_security` method in
`superset/initialization/__init__.py` placed alongside `check_websocket_secret` (`:1131`) and
wired into `init_app` at `:1336`. Reuse the existing `_log_config_warning` banner helper
(`:1062`).

- **Refuse to start** when `SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE == "None"` and `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE` is
  falsy, with the same `debug`/`TESTING` escape hatch that `check_secret_key:1097` and
  `check_websocket_secret:1146` already use. This combination has no valid deployment —
  every major browser discards the cookie — so refusing to start cannot break a working
  install.
- **Warn** when `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE` is falsy and the deployment looks like it is serving
  HTTPS, that is when `PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME == "https"` or `ENABLE_PROXY_FIX` is on.
  `PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME` is a Flask key, not a Superset one — it is absent from
  `superset/config.py` and reaches `app.config` as Flask's `"http"` default, so read it from
  `app.config` rather than expecting it in the config module.

No default changes. `config.py:2853` stays `False`. `docs/admin_docs/security/security.mdx:700`
is the one current page that documents that default, and it stays correct.
`docs/admin_docs/security/securing_superset.mdx:89` and
`docs/admin_docs/configuration/networking-settings.mdx:114` state the recommendation to set
`True`, which is a different claim and is unaffected either way. The HTTP login-loop
regression that got the flip reverted in apache/superset#26005 (issue #24579) cannot recur:
the plain-HTTP development path is `Lax`
plus `Secure=False` plus `http`, which hits neither tier.

Gating the default on a detected scheme is not viable and should not be attempted.
`superset/config.py` is a module executed at import time, and the `superset_config.py`
override at `config.py:3402-3421` does `setattr(module, key, ...)` for every uppercase name —
afterwards there is no way to distinguish "the operator explicitly set `False`" from "the
default was `False`", so a conditional default would silently override an explicit choice.

While here, cover the websocket pair on the same invariant: `WEBSOCKET_JWT_COOKIE_SAMESITE`
and `WEBSOCKET_JWT_COOKIE_SECURE` (`config.py:3016-3017`), gated on `WEBSOCKET_ENABLE`
exactly as `check_websocket_secret:1133` already gates. Do not change those defaults either.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE="None"` with `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=False` on a non-test app
      raises `SystemExit(1)`, and the emitted log names both keys.
- [ ] The same combination with `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=True` starts clean, no warning.
- [ ] The shipped defaults (`Lax`, `False`, `http`) start clean: no warning, no exit.
- [ ] `PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME="https"` with `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=False` emits at least one
      `WARNING`-level record whose message contains the literal string
      `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE`, and does not exit. Assert on record content, not on a record
      count: `_log_config_warning` (`superset/initialization/__init__.py:1063-1067`) issues
      three `logger.warning` calls per message, a top banner, the message and a bottom banner,
      so any single-record assertion is unsatisfiable by the fix this issue asks for.
- [ ] Under `TESTING` or debug the invalid combination warns but does not exit, matching the
      contract of the existing checks.
- [ ] With `WEBSOCKET_ENABLE=True`, `WEBSOCKET_JWT_COOKIE_SAMESITE="None"` and
      `WEBSOCKET_JWT_COOKIE_SECURE=False` behaves the same way; with `WEBSOCKET_ENABLE=False`
      it is not checked at all.
- [ ] The shipped values of `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE` (`False`), `SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE`
      (`"Lax"`), `WEBSOCKET_JWT_COOKIE_SECURE` (`False`) and `WEBSOCKET_JWT_COOKIE_SAMESITE`
      (`None`) are unchanged. This constrains those four assignments and nothing else. Do not
      check it with a whole-file diff of `superset/config.py`: another issue in this queue adds
      a key next to `CSV_STREAMING_ROW_THRESHOLD` (`config.py:1530-1534`), so a file-level
      probe would fail for reasons that have nothing to do with this change.

Note for whoever writes the tests: `tests/unit_tests/conftest.py:95` sets
`app.config["PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME="]` — the key literal has a stray trailing `=` inside the
string, so that line creates a junk key and never sets the scheme. Do not inherit it and
assume it works.

issues.title: extract_errors: OceanBase CONNECTION_UNKNOWN_DATABASE mapping is untested
issues.body:
`superset/db_engine_specs/oceanbase.py` maps the driver string `Unknown database '...'` to `SupersetErrorType.CONNECTION_UNKNOWN_DATABASE_ERROR` (`CONNECTION_UNKNOWN_DATABASE_REGEX` at line 39, wired into the error map at 190-192). No test runs a driver string through `OceanBaseEngineSpec.extract_errors` and checks the result. If the regex or the mapping entry changes, a user pointed at a database that does not exist would get a raw driver dump instead of the friendly error, and CI would stay green.

Fix: add a unit test under `tests/unit_tests/db_engine_specs/` that calls `extract_errors` with a message matching the spec's own regex and asserts the mapped error type. No production change.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The test feeds a driver string taken from the spec's own regex and asserts it maps to `CONNECTION_UNKNOWN_DATABASE_ERROR`, with the parsed database name present.
- [ ] The assertion fails if the regex-to-error-type entry is removed from the mapping.
- [ ] The `db_engine_specs` suite stays green.

issues.title: Streaming export chunk size hard-coded in two places (charts + SQL Lab)
issues.body:
The streaming export chunk size is hard-coded in two places, each under the same standing TODO:

- `superset/charts/data/api.py:802-803`
  ```python
  # TODO: Make chunk size configurable via SUPERSET_CONFIG
  chunk_size = 1024
  ```
- `superset/sqllab/api.py:437-438` — the same two lines, same value, same TODO.

Throughput cannot be tuned per deployment, and because the value is duplicated any change has to be made in both files. Fixing one and missing the other is the trap, so the fix routes both through a single config key.

Fix: add one config key (for example `CSV_EXPORT_CHUNK_SIZE`) next to `CSV_STREAMING_ROW_THRESHOLD` in `superset/config.py:1530-1534`, read at both call sites via `app.config.get(...)` — both modules already import `current_app as app`. When the key is unset, both sites use `1024` as today. Remove both TODOs.

Two things to get right:

- The command classes default to **1000**, not 1024 (`superset/commands/streaming_export/base.py:74`, mirrored in the sqllab and chart streaming export commands). Dropping the explicit argument at the API sites and letting the command default apply would silently change behavior 1024 → 1000, and the existing command tests assert 1000, so they would stay green. Both API sites must keep passing the config-derived value explicitly, defaulting to 1024.
- This key is backend-only. Do not add it to the frontend-exposed config tuple at `superset/views/base.py:138`.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One config key controls the chunk size at both `charts/data/api.py` and `sqllab/api.py`.
- [ ] With the key unset, both sites pass `1024` to their streaming export command (not 1000, and not the command's own default).
- [ ] A test asserts an overridden value reaches the command at both sites, and fails if either still reads a literal `1024`.
- [ ] Both `# TODO: Make chunk size configurable via SUPERSET_CONFIG` comments are gone.
- [ ] `tests/unit_tests/charts/` and `tests/unit_tests/sqllab/` are green.

issues.title: js-yaml resolves below 4.3.2 (GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh / CVE-2026-84375, HIGH)
issues.body:
`js-yaml` 4.x resolves below 4.3.2 in `superset-frontend/package-lock.json`. Versions `>=4.0.0 <4.3.2` are affected by GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh (CVE-2026-84375, HIGH, CVSS 7.5) — `maxTotalMergeKeys` does not limit CPU use for empty merge sources, so crafted YAML causes uncontrolled CPU consumption. Patched in 4.3.2.

There are **four** vulnerable resolutions, all at 4.3.1:

- `node_modules/cosmiconfig/node_modules/js-yaml` — package-lock.json:19797
- `node_modules/lerna/node_modules/js-yaml` — package-lock.json:31750
- `node_modules/react-diff-viewer-continued/node_modules/js-yaml` — package-lock.json:38825
- `node_modules/stylelint/node_modules/js-yaml` — package-lock.json:42497

The first three have `"js-yaml": "^4.3.1"` override entries in `superset-frontend/package.json` (lines 399, 422, 431). **`stylelint` does not** — it carries its own `"js-yaml": "^4.1.0"` dependency (package-lock.json:42397) with no override. A fix that only re-resolves the three overridden blocks leaves the fourth vulnerable and fails the acceptance criteria below.

The `^4.3.1` caret ranges already permit 4.3.2, so no manifest bump is required for the three overrides; this is a lockfile refresh (`npm update js-yaml --package-lock-only`, or an added `stylelint` override if the update does not reach it).

The two `js-yaml@^3.x` override entries (package.json:387 `@istanbuljs/load-nyc-config`, package.json:418 `js-yaml-loader`) need no change, but not because 3.x is unaffected — the same advisory covers `>=3.0.0 <3.15.2`. They are safe only because the lockfile already resolves both to 3.15.2 (package-lock.json:4814, :30838). The refresh must not regress them below that.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every resolved `js-yaml` 4.x entry in `superset-frontend/package-lock.json` is 4.3.2 or later — all four listed above, `stylelint` included.
- [ ] Every resolved `js-yaml` 3.x entry stays at 3.15.2 or later.
- [ ] A static check over the lockfile finds no resolved `js-yaml` in `[4.0.0, 4.3.2)` or `[3.0.0, 3.15.2)`.
- [ ] `npm ci` and `npm run build` succeed against the refreshed lockfile.
- [ ] `npm audit` no longer reports GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh.

issues.title: KQL splitter drops all text before a triple-backtick string, merging or destroying statements
issues.body:
The KQL statement splitter loses the text before a triple-backtick multiline string. In `superset/sql/parse.py`, `tokenize_kql` (called by `split_kql`, `parse.py:1830`; the call is at `:1835`) builds a statement in `buffer`, but on entering a multiline string it overwrites the buffer instead of flushing it:

```python
# parse.py:1795-1797 — in tokenize_kql
elif ch == "`" and script[i - 2 : i] == "``":
    state = KQLSplitState.INSIDE_MULTILINE_STRING
    buffer = "```"   # discards everything accumulated before the ``` opener
```

The single- and double-quote branch immediately above (:1785-1794) flushes correctly (`tokens.extend(classify_non_string_kql(buffer)); buffer = ""`), which is what makes the multiline branch a bug rather than a design choice.

Observed, running the splitter directly:

```
IN : print program = ```hello```
OUT: ['```hello```']                       # "print program = " is gone

IN : let x = 1; print program = ```he;llo``` | take 2
OUT: ['```he;llo``` | take 2']             # 1 statement, not 2 — "let x = 1" destroyed
```

So it is not only a truncated statement: an earlier complete statement and its separator are swallowed, changing the number of statements returned. The truncated result flows to execution through `_parse_statement`/`format()`, so a valid script is silently corrupted before it runs.

The existing test `test_kustokqlstatement_with_program` (`tests/unit_tests/sql/parse_tests.py:1533-1549`) asserts only `len(statements) == 1` and never checks the content, so the bug passes today. None of the `test_split_kql` parametrize cases contain triple backticks.

Fix: on entering `INSIDE_MULTILINE_STRING`, flush the accumulated prefix (`buffer[:-2]` — the part before the two backticks already consumed) into the token stream before switching state.

Coverage note: `.github/workflows/superset-python-unittest.yml:82` runs `superset/sql/` under `--cov-fail-under=100` with `branch = True` in `.coveragerc`. A guarded `if buffer[:-2]:` adds a branch that then needs both sides covered. `classify_non_string_kql("")` returns `[]`, so the branchless flush satisfies the gate without extra cases.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test splits `print program = ` followed by a triple-backtick string and asserts the returned statement text still contains `print program =` along with the string literal.
- [ ] A test splits `let x = 1; print program = ` followed by a triple-backtick string containing a `;` and asserts two statements are returned, with `let x = 1` intact.
- [ ] Both tests fail against the current `buffer = "```"` overwrite and pass once the prefix is flushed.
- [ ] `tests/unit_tests/sql/parse_tests.py` is green and `superset/sql/` still meets `--cov-fail-under=100` under branch coverage.

issues.title: "end of this quarter" raises ValueError in the freeform date parser
issues.body:
`end of this quarter` raises `ValueError` in the freeform date parser instead of resolving.

`handle_end_of` (`superset/utils/date_parser.py:311-313`) accepts `quarter` and emits `LASTDAY(<date>, quarter)`. The `LASTDAY` grammar does not accept it:

```python
Group(date_expr + comma + (YEAR | MONTH | WEEK) + ppOptional(comma))   # date_parser.py:944
```

`EvalLastDayFunc.eval` (`date_parser.py:829-847`) has no quarter branch either, so both the grammar and the evaluator need the unit.

Running the real parser with `today` pinned to 2016-11-07:

```
handle_end_of("DATETIME('today')", 'quarter') -> LASTDAY(DATETIME('today'), quarter)
parse LASTDAY(DATETIME('today'), quarter)     -> ParseException: Expected lastday, found 'quarter' (col 28)
datetime_eval                                  -> ValueError: Expected lastday, found 'quarter'
parse LASTDAY(DATETIME('today'), month)        -> OK
```

`DATEADD` (`:925`) and `DATETRUNC` (`:936`) both list `QUARTER` in their unit alternations, and start-of-quarter resolves through `DATETRUNC` without error. Only the end-of form fails, on an expression the modifier regex at `:586-589` explicitly admits.

Scope note: only the qualified forms (`end of this|last|next|prior quarter`) reach `handle_end_of` through that regex. A bare `end of quarter` takes a different path and is out of scope here.

Fix: add `QUARTER` to the `LASTDAY` alternation and add the matching branch to `EvalLastDayFunc.eval` so `LASTDAY(date, quarter)` returns the last day of that quarter. Leave the other units and start-of-quarter alone.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With the suite's frozen today of 2016-11-07, `get_since_until("end of this quarter : ")` returns `(datetime(2016, 12, 31), None)` instead of raising.
- [ ] The new test raises `ValueError` against current HEAD and passes once `QUARTER` is wired through both the grammar and the eval branch.
- [ ] Existing `tests/unit_tests/utils/date_parser_tests.py` cases stay green, including start-of-quarter and end-of month/year/week. Run with `TZ=UTC`.

issues.title: Custom-tags mixin's substring rewrite of the rison `q` corrupts filter values and is not idempotent
issues.body:
`superset/views/custom_tags_api_mixin.py:86-103` rewrites the `q` query string by substring replacement before handing it to FAB:

```python
86:  query_str = request.args.get("q", "")
87:  if query_str and "tags." in query_str:
89:      modified_query = query_str.replace("tags.id", "custom_tags.id")
90:      modified_query = modified_query.replace("tags.name", "custom_tags.name")
91:      modified_query = modified_query.replace("tags.type", "custom_tags.type")
```

`q` is rison, and this treats it as text. Running those three replacements over the rison FAB actually emits:

```
value contains the literal text:
  (filters:!((col:dashboard_title,opr:title_or_slug,value:'tags.name migration')))
  -> (filters:!((col:dashboard_title,opr:title_or_slug,value:'custom_tags.name migration')))

another relation ending in "tags":
  (columns:!(owner_tags.id,mytags.name))
  -> (columns:!(owner_custom_tags.id,mycustom_tags.name))

already-rewritten input:
  (columns:!(custom_tags.id))
  -> (columns:!(custom_custom_tags.id))

a tags column outside the hard-coded three:
  (columns:!(tags.description))   unchanged, so it stays unresolvable against list_columns
```

The first case is reachable from the UI: the dashboard list search box sends free text as a `dashboard_title` filter with operator `title_or_slug` (`FilterOperator.TitleOrSlug` at `superset-frontend/src/pages/DashboardList/index.tsx:661`, enum value at `superset-frontend/src/components/ListView/types.ts:126`, resolved server-side by `DashboardTitleOrSlugFilter`, `superset/dashboards/filters.py:45-47`), and the same list request carries the tag columns (`DashboardList/index.tsx:170-172`), so a user searching for the literal string `tags.name` silently gets results for `custom_tags.name`. The third case makes the method non-idempotent — a client that already sends `custom_tags.id` gets `custom_custom_tags.id` and a 400 from FAB.

The live consumer is `DashboardRestApi` (`superset/dashboards/api.py:303`, configured at `:365`).

Existing coverage does not reach this path. `tests/unit_tests/views/test_custom_tags_api_mixin.py` has five tests, all on `_init_model_schemas` and `pre_get_list`; none reference `get_list`, `request.args`, or `q`.

Fix: parse `q` with `prison` (already pinned at `requirements/base.txt:286` and used in-tree at `superset/utils/rison_filters.py:28`), rewrite the column names in the parsed structure — `columns`, `select_columns`, `order_column`, and `filters[].col` — and re-serialize. Leave filter values alone. On a parse failure, pass the original `q` through untouched so FAB's existing error handling still applies. Decide explicitly whether `tags.<other>` columns are rewritten or left alone, and state the choice in the code.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given `q=(filters:!((col:dashboard_title,opr:title_or_slug,value:'tags.name migration')))`, the shape the dashboard list UI sends, the filter value seen by `super().get_list()` still parses to `tags.name migration`.
- [ ] Given `q=(columns:!(id,tags.name,tags.id,tags.type))`, the parsed `columns` are `["id","custom_tags.name","custom_tags.id","custom_tags.type"]`.
- [ ] Given `q=(columns:!(owner_tags.id))`, `columns` parses to `["owner_tags.id"]` — no substring bleed into unrelated relations.
- [ ] Given `q=(columns:!(custom_tags.id))`, `columns` parses to `["custom_tags.id"]`, so the rewrite is idempotent.
- [ ] `q=(columns:!(tags.description))` behaves per the documented choice, asserted explicitly either way.
- [ ] A malformed `q` such as `(columns:!(tags.id` is passed through unmodified rather than raising inside the mixin.
- [ ] Assertions are made on the parsed structure, not on the raw string, so serialization differences do not make the tests brittle.

issues.title: WebSocket JWT cookie not Secure / SameSite None
issues.body:
The websocket JWT cookie ships with insecure defaults. `superset/config.py:3013-3014`:

```python
WEBSOCKET_JWT_COOKIE_SECURE = False
WEBSOCKET_JWT_COOKIE_SAMESITE: None | (Literal["None", "Lax", "Strict"]) = None
```

`superset/websocket/channel.py:225-234` passes both straight to Flask's `set_cookie`. With `secure=False` the cookie carries no `Secure` attribute and will ride over plain HTTP. With `samesite=None` (Python `None`, not the string `"None"`) Werkzeug omits the `SameSite` attribute entirely, so the cookie's cross-site behavior is left to whatever the browser defaults to — Lax in Chromium, not uniformly enforced elsewhere.

Two things this issue is not claiming. This is not an undiscovered exposure: `superset-websocket/README.md:196-209` already lists setting `WEBSOCKET_JWT_COOKIE_SECURE = True` and choosing an explicit SameSite under "Production hardening checklist". And the blast radius on a stock install is zero, because `WEBSOCKET_ENABLE` defaults to `False` (`config.py:3009`) and `superset/initialization/__init__.py:1625-1630` only registers the cookie hook when it is on. The argument is that an operator who turns websockets on should get a secure cookie without having to read a separate README, in the same way issue #1 argues for the session cookie.

Fix: default `WEBSOCKET_JWT_COOKIE_SECURE` to `True` and `WEBSOCKET_JWT_COOKIE_SAMESITE` to `"Lax"`, both still overridable from `superset_config.py`. Add an `UPDATING.md` entry, because cross-site websocket deployments need `"None"` and must set it explicitly.

The existing test at `tests/unit_tests/websocket/test_channel.py:136-146` builds its own Flask app and hardcodes `WEBSOCKET_JWT_COOKIE_SECURE=False, WEBSOCKET_JWT_COOKIE_SAMESITE=None`. It never reads the shipped defaults, so it passes whatever `config.py` says and gives no signal here. A test asserting the new values are set is equally empty — it greps its own diff. The criteria below are behavioral for that reason.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With `WEBSOCKET_ENABLE=True` and otherwise default config, the `Set-Cookie` header for the websocket token on an authenticated response carries `Secure` and `SameSite=Lax`, read off a real response rather than asserted against `config.py`.
- [ ] A `superset_config.py` override back to `WEBSOCKET_JWT_COOKIE_SECURE=False` and `WEBSOCKET_JWT_COOKIE_SAMESITE="None"` still takes effect on the emitted header.
- [ ] The existing `test_channel.py` fixture is not deleted or weakened; its hardcoded values may stay, and the new coverage exercises the shipped defaults instead.
- [ ] `UPDATING.md` records the changed defaults and names `"None"` as the setting cross-site deployments must restore.

issues.title: machine_auth priming page is never closed; upstream reports the leaked page can clobber the injected session cookie (apache/superset#44005)
issues.body:
Upstream issue: https://github.com/apache/superset/issues/44005 (open, unassigned, no linked
PR). Carried into this fork because the condition is present here and the remediation is
bounded.

`MachineAuthProvider.authenticate_browser_context` (`machine_auth.py:53`) opens a page to prime the browser context and
never closes it. `superset/utils/machine_auth.py:64-66`:

```python
# Setting cookies requires doing a request first
page = browser_context.new_page()
page.goto(headless_url("/login/"))
```

`grep -n "close()" superset/utils/machine_auth.py` returns nothing. The page is still live
when `browser_context.clear_cookies()` and `add_cookies(...)` run at `:70-83`, and it stays
open for the life of the context.

This issue proves the leak: the page is opened, never closed, and the existing test never
checks for it. The race is upstream's finding, reported in apache/superset#44005: the login
SPA keeps making requests after `page.goto()` returns, and a late
`Set-Cookie: session=<anonymous>` overwrites the injected cookie in the shared jar, so report
screenshots land on the login screen. The ordering is not deterministic. `goto()` here uses the
default `wait_until="load"`, which Playwright documents as "consider operation to be finished
when the `load` event is fired"; it says nothing about in-flight XHRs, and the `/login/` page
is a Superset SPA that keeps talking to the server after load. So the window is real, but it
was not reproduced in this fork and none of the criteria below depend on it. Closing the page
(or not opening one) before `add_cookies` fixes the leak and closes that window with it.

The comment claims setting cookies requires a request first. That was true of Selenium.
Maintainer `rusackas` asked on the upstream issue whether the navigation can simply be
dropped, since Playwright's `BrowserContext.add_cookies` does not require a prior navigation.

Two acceptable fix shapes, and the criteria below accept either:
- Drop the navigation entirely.
- Keep it and close the page before injecting cookies.

Nearby but out of scope: PR #43253 (open) touches this file for a Playwright wait event, a
different symptom. Do not fold that in. It also edits
`tests/integration_tests/utils/machine_auth_tests.py`, so expect a conflict if it merges
first.

The existing test at `tests/integration_tests/utils/machine_auth_tests.py:31-50` mocks the
Playwright surface entirely — `MagicMock` context and page — and is the template. No
Playwright binary and no browser are needed. It is an integration test, though:
`MachineAuthProviderTests` (`:25`) extends `SupersetTestCase` and `self.get_user("admin")` at
`:33` queries the seeded test database, so this is not the fast unit lane.

Required lane: integration. Run through `scripts/tests/run.sh` with
`SUPERSET_CONFIG=tests.integration_tests.superset_test_config`, which does `superset db
upgrade`, `superset init` and `superset load-test-users` before pytest; this is the setup
`.github/workflows/superset-python-integrationtest.yml` uses. Under the `tests/unit_tests`
sqlite lane (`superset-python-unittest.yml:71`) the file fails on the missing `admin` user
before it reaches the defect.

Fix shape A also requires deleting `mock_page.goto.assert_called_once()` at
`machine_auth_tests.py:44`. That assertion encodes the behaviour being removed, so it will go
red — that is expected, not a regression the agent caused.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test builds a mock browser context with `mock_context.new_page.return_value =
      mock_page`, patches `get_cookies` to return `{"session": "abc123"}`, calls
      `authenticate_browser_context`, and asserts the injected cookie still reaches `add_cookies`.
- [ ] The same test asserts no priming page is left open: if `new_page` was called at all,
      `mock_page.close` was called exactly once.
- [ ] If a priming page is opened, a parent mock recording call order shows `close` is called
      before `add_cookies`. If the navigation is dropped entirely, `new_page` is never called
      and this criterion is vacuous — do not force a page open to satisfy it.
- [ ] The test fails against current HEAD and passes under either fix shape.
- [ ] `_auth_webdriver_func_override` (`:58-60`) still short-circuits before any of this.

issues.title: versioning/diff.py drops and fabricates chart-history records when two adhoc filters share a column
issues.body:
Chart-history records are silently dropped, and sometimes fabricated, when a chart has two
adhoc filters on the same column.

`_diff_list_by_natural_key` (`superset/versioning/diff.py:425-430`) indexes both sides of a
list by a natural key with no collision handling:

```python
from_by_key: dict[Key, Any] = {}
for idx, item in enumerate(from_list):
    from_by_key[_effective_key(key_fn(item), idx)] = item
```

For adhoc filters the key is the filter's `subject`, the column name (`_filter_key`,
`:481-490`). Two filters on one column is the most common filter shape there is — a numeric
range is `x >= a` plus `x <= b` — and the second one overwrites the first before any record
is emitted.

The docstring on `_filter_key` claims a mitigation the code cannot provide:

> Users rarely have two filters on the same column; when they do the secondary dimensions
> (operator, comparator) appear in the record's from/to values so the renderer can
> disambiguate.

They cannot appear. The overwritten item is gone from the dict before the diff runs.

Observed, running the module against filters `sales > 1` and `sales < 10`:

| user action | records emitted | correct |
|---|---|---|
| delete `sales > 1` | `[]` | one `remove` |
| edit `sales > 1` to `sales > 5` | `[]` | one `edit` |
| add `sales != 7` | one `edit` claiming `sales < 10` **became** `sales != 7` | one `add` |

So the audit log both loses real edits and reports a change that never happened. Control
cases behave correctly: a single-filter edit produces one `edit`, and two filters on
different columns with one deleted produces one `remove`.

`_diff_list_by_natural_key` is the shared child-collection walker for `diff_slice_params`
(filters, metrics, dimensions), `diff_dataset_columns`, and `diff_dataset_metrics`. Dataset
columns and metrics key on unique names and are safe. Chart `metrics` keyed on `label` and
`groupby`/`columns` keyed on the dimension string are exposed the same way, less often.
Records reach `version_changes` through `superset/versioning/changes/state.py:232`.

There is no existing coverage. `tests/unit_tests/versioning/` has no `test_diff.py`. In `test_diff_caps.py` the
filter fixture at `:81-82` uses `{"col": ..., "val": ...}` items with no `subject`, so it takes
the positional-index fallback and never reaches `_filter_key`; the `_REALISTIC_PARAMS` fixture
at `:155-164` does carry `subject`, but every subject is a distinct `dim_{i}`, so no collision
is ever exercised.

Fix: give duplicate natural keys a stable identity. The choice is the work — an identity has
to survive reordering (that is the whole reason for keying naturally rather than positionally)
while still separating two filters on one column. Decide also whether this belongs in
`_filter_key` or in `_diff_list_by_natural_key`'s collision handling; the latter also covers
metrics and dimensions. Whatever the shape, `path` must stay consumable by
`superset/versioning/schemas.py:398-399`, where it is a `fields.List(fields.String())`.
Correct the `_filter_key` docstring to describe what the code does.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With filters `sales > 1` and `sales < 10`, deleting the first yields exactly one
      `remove` record whose from-value is the deleted filter. Yields `[]` at HEAD.
- [ ] With the same pair, editing the first yields exactly one `edit` record from the old
      first filter to the new one. Yields `[]` at HEAD.
- [ ] With the same pair, adding `sales != 7` yields an `add` record and **no** record
      claiming one surviving filter turned into another. Fabricates an `edit` at HEAD.
- [ ] Reorder guard: swapping the order of two filters on **different** columns, with no
      other change, still yields no records. A fix that falls back to positional keys breaks
      this, so it is what makes the criteria above non-tautological.
- [ ] A single-filter edit still yields one `edit` at path `["params","adhoc_filters","sales"]`.
- [ ] Two filters on different columns, one deleted, still yields one `remove`.
- [ ] `tests/unit_tests/versioning/test_diff_caps.py` is unchanged and green.

issues.title: nx pins brace-expansion 5.0.8 (GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895); the minimatch override has the wrong parent and a stale floor
issues.body:
`superset-frontend/package-lock.json` resolves `node_modules/nx/node_modules/brace-expansion` at 5.0.8. GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895 (CVE-2026-69152, HIGH, CVSS 7.5, `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`, CWE-400/CWE-770) covers `>=4.0.0 <5.0.9`; first patched version is 5.0.9. Crafted brace patterns build unbounded intermediate arrays, bypassing the earlier CVE-2026-14257 mitigation. Verified with `gh api /advisories/GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895`.

Every other resolved `brace-expansion` in the lockfile is already on a patched line: the hoisted `node_modules/brace-expansion` is 5.0.9, the seven jest-related nested copies are 2.1.4 (patched at 2.1.4), and `node_modules/minimatch/node_modules/brace-expansion` is 1.1.18 (patched at 1.1.18). The `nx` copy is the only vulnerable one.

### Why it is stuck

`nx@23.1.1` declares `brace-expansion` as an exact pin, not a range:

```
$ npm view nx@23.1.1 dependencies.brace-expansion
5.0.8
```

so no lockfile refresh at that `nx` version can move it. `nx` itself is not pinned. It arrives through `lerna@10.0.1` (`package.json:329`, `"lerna": "^10.0.1"`, a devDependency), whose declared range is `"nx": ">=23.1.0 < 24.0.0"`. `nx@23.1.2`, published 2026-08-26, is the first release that pins 5.0.9:

```
$ npm view nx@23.1.2 dependencies.brace-expansion
5.0.9
```

So a lockfile re-resolution of `nx` inside the existing `lerna` range does clear the vulnerable copy; no manifest change is needed for that half. `nx` is a dependency of `lerna` only (`@nx/devkit` peer-depends on it, and is itself a `lerna` dependency); `lerna` is a devDependency, so this is build-time tooling and never ships to the browser.

### The override does not help

`package.json:424-426`:

```json
"minimatch@>=10": {
  "brace-expansion": ">=5.0.8"
},
```

This misses twice. The parent is wrong: the vulnerable copy is a direct dependency of `nx`, not of `minimatch`. All twenty `minimatch@10.x` copies in the tree declare `brace-expansion` as `^5.0.5` or `^5.0.8` and already resolve to the hoisted 5.0.9. And the floor is stale: `>=5.0.8` admits 5.0.8, which is inside the advisory's range, so even with the right parent it would not force a fix. It also cannot reach `nx`'s exact pin from the wrong parent, so today it is a no-op for this advisory.

### Fix

Two independent parts.

1. Re-resolve `nx` to `>=23.1.2` within the `lerna` range (`npm update nx --package-lock-only`, or equivalent). This is what removes the vulnerable copy.
2. Edit the override in `package.json` so it stops documenting a floor that admits a vulnerable version. Either raise the floor to `>=5.0.9`, or remove the entry if it no longer serves a purpose once every `minimatch@10` resolves to 5.0.9 through its own caret. State which in the PR. This part is a `package.json` edit and cannot be produced by re-resolution.

Do not add an override keyed on `nx` as a substitute for part 1. Overriding an exact pin works, but it hides the fact that the upstream fix is already inside the allowed `lerna` range, and it would need to be removed again later.

### Acceptance criteria

Vulnerable copy (part 1):
- [ ] `node_modules/nx` in `superset-frontend/package-lock.json` resolves to a version `>=23.1.2 <24.0.0`, inside the `lerna` range, with no change to the `lerna` entry in `package.json`.
- [ ] No `brace-expansion` entry in `package-lock.json` resolves to a version in `[4.0.0, 5.0.9)`. Check resolved versions with a static pass over the lockfile, not with `npm audit`; a clean audit is not evidence on its own.
- [ ] The 2.x and 1.x copies stay at `>=2.1.4` and `>=1.1.18` respectively.

Override floor (part 2):
- [ ] `package.json` no longer contains an override whose `brace-expansion` floor admits 5.0.8. Either the `minimatch@>=10` entry reads `>=5.0.9` or the entry is gone.

Both:
- [ ] `npm ci` and `npm run build` succeed in `superset-frontend/` against the refreshed lockfile.

Not a criterion: whether `node_modules/nx/node_modules/brace-expansion` still exists as a nested entry. Once `nx` pins 5.0.9 npm may dedupe it onto the hoisted 5.0.9, and that is correct.

issues.title: nx pins brace-expansion 5.0.8 (GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895); the minimatch override has the wrong parent and a stale floor
issues.body:
## Summary

Two independent defects in `superset-frontend/` leave the dev dependency tree resolving a `brace-expansion` copy inside the range of [GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895) (CVE-2026-69152, **HIGH**, CVSS 7.5 — DoS via unbounded intermediate arrays, bypassing the CVE-2026-14257 mitigation). Affected ranges: `<1.1.18`, `>=2.0.0 <2.1.4`, `>=3.0.0 <3.0.6`, `>=4.0.0 <5.0.9`.

Both halves are **build-time only**: `nx`, `@nx/devkit`, and `lerna` are all `dev: true` in the lockfile. Nothing here ships to runtime. (Per `SECURITY.md`, this is dependency hygiene in the dev toolchain, not a privilege/capability violation of the Superset security model.)

## Half one — the vulnerable copy (lockfile-only fix)

`package-lock.json` pins `node_modules/nx` at **23.1.1** (`dev: true`, entry begins at line 34777), and nx 23.1.1's own manifest **exact-pins** `brace-expansion: "5.0.8"` (line 34803). That produces a nested vulnerable resolution at `node_modules/nx/node_modules/brace-expansion@5.0.8` (line 35006) — inside the advisory's `>=4.0.0 <5.0.9` range.

- The other **8** brace-expansion resolutions in the lockfile are already patched (6× `2.1.4`, hoisted `5.0.9`, `1.1.18` under `node_modules/minimatch` — see reproduction comment).
- nx **is** re-resolvable inside its dependents' ranges: `node_modules/lerna` requires `nx >=23.1.0 <24.0.0` (line 31393) and `node_modules/@nx/devkit` peers `nx >= 22 <= 24 || ^23.0.0-0` (line 9009). `nx@23.1.2` is the first release carrying `brace-expansion@5.0.9` (`npm view nx@23.1.1 dependencies.brace-expansion` → `5.0.8`; `npm view nx@23.1.2 …` → `5.0.9`) — a patch bump, not 23.2.0.
- A plain `npm install` does **not** clear this: verified, `npm install --package-lock-only` produces a zero-line diff — npm honours the existing lock entry and leaves nx at 23.1.1. The lockfile must be re-resolved.

## Half two — the stale override floor (manifest fix)

`package.json` lines 424–426:

```json
"minimatch@>=10": {
  "brace-expansion": ">=5.0.8"
}
```

Two problems, verified:

1. **Wrong parent for this case.** npm override keys select the *dependent*. The edge that placed the vulnerable copy is `nx → brace-expansion` (nx's own exact pin), which a `minimatch`-scoped override cannot govern. Demonstrated empirically: with only the floor raised to `>=5.0.9`, npm 11 keeps `brace-expansion@5.0.8` under `node_modules/nx` (flagged `invalid`) and merely adds a *deeper* nested `node_modules/nx/node_modules/minimatch/node_modules/brace-expansion@5.0.9` — the nx edge itself is outside the override's reach.
2. **Stale floor.** `>=5.0.8` still admits `5.0.8`, which is inside the advisory range. Every `minimatch@10.2.5` in the tree declares `brace-expansion: ^5.0.5`, so the override floor is the only guard for those edges — and it currently *permits* the vulnerable version. Today `node_modules/nx/node_modules/minimatch@10.2.5` actually dedupes **into** the vulnerable 5.0.8 copy (`npm ls` shows `brace-expansion@5.0.8 deduped` under it), precisely because the floor admits it.

Note: `superset-frontend/cypress-base/package.json` already carries the corrected floor `"minimatch@>=10": {"brace-expansion": ">=5.0.9"}` (upstream PR apache/superset#43664) — the main `superset-frontend` manifest was left behind. The same defect is present on current upstream `apache/superset@master`.

## Acceptance criteria

Verify by **resolution**, not by `npm audit` — an audit that reports clean is not sufficient evidence (advisory DB lag); enumerate the resolved versions in the lockfile.

**Half one — vulnerable copy (a lockfile-only change may satisfy these):**

- [ ] Every `*node_modules/brace-expansion` entry in `superset-frontend/package-lock.json` resolves outside all four GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895 ranges (i.e. `>=1.1.18 <2`, `>=2.1.4 <3`, `>=3.0.6 <4`, or `>=5.0.9`).
- [ ] `node_modules/nx` resolves to a release whose own `brace-expansion` requirement is already patched (first such: `23.1.2`), while remaining within every dependent's range (`lerna`: `>=23.1.0 <24.0.0`; `@nx/devkit` peer: `>= 22 <= 24 || ^23.0.0-0`) and `dev: true`.
- [ ] `npm ls` reports the tree cleanly — no `invalid` marker on any `brace-expansion` edge.

**Half two — stale override floor (requires the manifest edit):**

- [ ] No `brace-expansion` floor inside `package.json` `overrides` admits a version inside the advisory ranges: the `minimatch@>=10` floor reads `>=5.0.9`.
- [ ] The edge that placed the vulnerable copy is governed by the correct parent: `overrides` includes `"nx": { "brace-expansion": ">=5.0.9" }`, so any future nx that re-pins a vulnerable `brace-expansion` surfaces as `invalid` in `npm ls` instead of resolving silently.

Explicitly **not** a criterion: the nested `node_modules/nx/node_modules/brace-expansion` entry need not survive — once the hoisted copy satisfies nx's spec, npm correctly dedupes it away.

## File surface

`superset-frontend/package.json`, `superset-frontend/package-lock.json` only.
